verdict.rationale: Homebrew ships its own export: `brew bundle dump` snapshots installed formulae, casks, taps and other supported package types into a plain-text Brewfile. That Brewfile can be committed and reused, and `brew info --json` output provides machine-readable package metadata. However, the export covers only 'supported' package types, and there is no documented end-to-end exit or uninstall path. missing for 10: evidence that the export covers all user state (e.g. config or pinned versions), a documented full-uninstall/leave procedure, independent hands-on corroboration of the export round-trip

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: `brew bundle dump` is Homebrew's installed-state snapshot command: it records supported installed formulae, casks, taps and other package types as a `Brewfile`.
`Brewfile`s can also be used as a way of saving all supported packages into a single file.
List the `brew info --json` output for all current Homebrew/homebrew-core formulae or Homebrew/homebrew-cask casks.
